title: Improve autoscaler burst controls: edge-case smoothing and utilization reporting fixes
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Context: customers running Dedicated fleets observed tail latency spikes and incorrect burst utilization reporting when transient traffic spikes coincide with token-bucket refills. This PR tightens burst smoothing, fixes a race in the token-bucket accounting, and corrects reporting jitter that caused utilization to exceed the configured burst window in dashboards.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a smoothing window to the burst allowance decay so brief back-to-back spikes don't immediately drain capacity; 2) Fixes a concurrency bug in tokenbucket refills that could double-count capacity on rare interleavings; 3) Adds a deterministic sample-and-aggregate path in util_reporter to remove intermittent reporting jitter; 4) Adds integration tests that simulate bursty traffic overlapping autoscaler scaling events; 5) Updates docs with recommended tuning defaults.

Motivation: customers want predictable throughput guarantees and accurate utilization graphs for debugging SLA incidents. Previous behavior produced confusing utilization >100% artifacts in the console and occasional unjustified scaling decisions.

Notes: this is a targeted change (no model/runtime changes). It touches the autoscaler controller, token-bucket implementation, and the utilization reporter. Follow-up work will evaluate adaptive smoothing based on workload shape (ENG-1499).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] e2e simulation scenario for burst overlap
- [x] Metrics/trace spans added for investigation
- [x] Docs updated (dedicated/autoscaling tuning)

Related: ENG-1423, SUP-3281, previous burst work PRs: pr-362999, pr-424200.
